content:
emma: Quick follow-up on the FlowGate proposal — we need to lock the fallback boundary semantics before the next RFC iteration.

raj: Agreed. Main question: does FlowGate own the decision surface (pass/fail + target) or only emit signals to the Arbiter?

sophia: My read: FlowGate should be the local decisioner (fast path) and Arbiter is the long-lived adjudicator. FlowGate must make sub-100ms decisions for live requests.

marta: That implies FlowGate needs a small, stable signal set: latency P95, error rate, token drop, confidence delta. Anything else risks thrashing.

kai: Also we need to decide the fallback granularity — per-request, per-session, per-tenant. Per-request is safest but expensive to route. Per-session reduces churn but can violate freshness of signals.

emma: Proposal: default = per-session stickiness for 5m, fall back to per-request when error spikes > 5% in 1m window. Keeps overhead low but reactive.

raj: Sounds sensible. How does the smoothing interact with autoscaler? If FlowGate flips a ton of sessions to fallback, autoscaler might see increased demand and spin up. We could add a damping multiplier to the metric emitted to the control plane.

sophia: Right — FlowGate should annotate signals with "local_override" flag so control plane discounts them in autoscaling heuristics.

marta: We should be explicit about fallback types: degrade-model (smaller variant), route-to-old (previous stable), and stall (queue). Each has different cost/latency profiles.

kai: For degrade-model we need model-size compatibility checks. If KV cache layout differs, degrade-model is not safe. Should FlowGate check model-compatibility or ask Arbiter?

emma: Practical: FlowGate has a lightweight compatibility table (model aliases -> compatible fallbacks). It's synced from the control plane every minute. If no entry, fallback = route-to-old.

raj: Example config sketch: 
```
flowgate:
  sticky_session_ttl: 300s
  spike_threshold: 0.05 # 5% errors in 60s
  smoothing: ewma_alpha: 0.2
  fallback_priority: [degrade-model, route-to-old, stall]
  compatibility_ttl: 60s
```

sophia: Love that. One more: circuit guard. If a model experiences sustained mild errors (3% over 10m) we should open a slow-warm circuit that rejects canary traffic incrementally rather than immediate cutover.

marta: Practically we can implement three circuit states: CLOSED (normal), SOFT_OPEN (surgically reduce traffic using probed tokens), HARD_OPEN (route all to fallback). Transitions are signal-driven with hysteresis.

kai: What about observability and tooling? We need per-tenant trace id mapping to see which sessions were sticky-switched. Also a telemetry contract: FlowGate emits compact events: {session_id, cause, from_variant, to_variant, metric_snapshot}.

emma: Keep payload small, no traces of prompt content. PII-free. We'll use existing telemetry proto but add flowgate_reason enum.

deploy-bot: deploy request: canary/flowgate v0.3 -> staging at 2026-04-02T09:00Z. CI: green. :rocket:

raj: One operational concern — rapid oscillation when two nearby nodes disagree on sticky_session_ttl. Need cluster-wide reconciliation: Arbiter periodically runs a pass to reconcile session assignments for long-lived sessions (>15m).

sophia: Also add a debug endpoint to force-evaluate FlowGate for a session (non-production flag) to reproduce. Helps SREs.

marta: Security/privilege: only ops and infra roles can change compatibility table. We should gate that behind audit logs.

kai: Testing plan: unit tests for state machine, integration test with canary harness (synthetic spike + recovery), and a simulation that runs 100k sessions to check oscillation.

emma: Action items:
- raj: mock autoscaler interaction with "local_override" flag (PR)
- sophia: add flowgate_reason enum to telemetry proto and size-check payload (PR)
- marta: write SOFT_OPEN/HARD_OPEN state machine tests (ticket)
- kai: add compatibility TTL sync and debug endpoint (PR)

emma: TL;DR: FlowGate = fast local decisioner, small signal set, sticky-by-default w/ per-request escape, flags control-plane via annotated signals, three-state circuit guard, model-compatibility table sync. We'll fold these into the next RFC draft. :white_check_mark:

raj: minor nit — can we make sticky_session_ttl configurable per-tenant? large tenants might want longer stickiness.

sophia: Yes, make it overridable via tenant policy; default remains 5m.

emma: Perfect. I'll update the RFC section and schedule a follow-up sync next week.

marta: +1. Thanks all. :clap:
